title: Monte Carlo error-budget forecaster and runway simulator
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a Monte Carlo–based error-budget forecaster and runway simulator that predicts SLO breach probability over configurable horizons and surfaces actionable guidance (e.g., throttle suggestions, canary holdbacks, initiative gating). The output will feed the Console risk panel, power alert throttles, and drive an initiative runway view for PM/eng prioritization.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype produces probabilistic breach curves (P(breach) over time) for at least three representative SLIs: p95 latency, request success rate, and model-worker OOM rate.
Simulator ingests historical SLI time-series from the reliability telemetry pipeline and preserves seasonality and burst characteristics in samples.
Console shows a visual runway widget displaying median, 5th and 95th percentile runway length and an actionable recommendation (allowlist/hold) per initiative.
Automated playbook is created: when 7-day P(breach) > 10% THEN throttle new rollout + notify oncall + create follow-up initiative card.
Validation: backtest on last 18 months of incidents with AUC >= 0.78 for breach-classification and median runway prediction error < 15%.
Performance: simulation completes for a customer slice (90th percentile load) within 45s for interactive Console queries and within 15 minutes for full-tenant batch runs.
Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked to on-call runbooks and release checklist.

risks: Telemetry data fidelity: missing tags or inconsistent SLI definitions across services can bias probability estimates.
Compute cost: Monte Carlo ensemble for full-tenant batch forecasting may be expensive; need early perf guardrails.
Operator trust: false positives could cause unnecessary rollbacks; will require careful calibration and UX explainability.
Dependency on ENG-1842: without improved aggregation endpoints we cannot meet interactive latency targets.
